record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.context_brief: Arithmetic weights in pointwise ergodic averages
record.original_question: Let T be a measure-preserving transformation, f and g bounded measurable, Λ the von Mangoldt function, and φ a multiplicative function taking values in the unit disk and having convergent means on every arithmetic progression. Do the weighted double averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N Λ(n) f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) and (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N φ(n) f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) converge for almost every x?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Let (X, X , µ, T) be a system and f, g ∈ L∞(µ) be functions. If Λ is the von Mangoldt function and φ is a multiplicative function that takes values on the complex unit disc and has convergent means, then show that the averages (1/N) ΣN n=1 Λ(n) f(T^n x) · g(T^2n x) and the averages (1/N) ΣN n=1 φ(n) f(T^n x) · g(T^2n x) converge pointwise almost everywhere.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ be a measure-preserving system, where $T:X\to X$ is an invertible measure-preserving transformation of the probability space $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$. Let $f,g\in L^\infty(\mu)$.

(a) Let $\Lambda:\mathbb{N}\to[0,\infty)$ denote the von Mangoldt function, defined by $\Lambda(n)=\log p$ if $n=p^k$ for some prime $p$ and integer $k\ge 1$, and $\Lambda(n)=0$ otherwise. Prove or disprove that the limit
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\Lambda(n)\,f(T^n x)\,g(T^{2n} x)$$
exists for $\mu$-almost every $x\in X$.

(b) Let $\varphi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a multiplicative function (i.e. $\varphi(mn)=\varphi(m)\varphi(n)$ whenever $\gcd(m,n)=1$) taking values in the closed unit disc $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|\le 1\}$, and assume that $\varphi$ has convergent mean values on every arithmetic progression, i.e. for every $a,q\in\mathbb{N}$ the limit
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{\substack{n=1\\ n\equiv a\,(q)}}^{N}\varphi(n)$$
exists. Prove or disprove that
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\varphi(n)\,f(T^n x)\,g(T^{2n} x)$$
exists for $\mu$-almost every $x\in X$.
artifact.category_tag: multiple ergodic averages with arithmetic weights
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has established pointwise a.e. convergence of bilinear ergodic averages of the form (1/N) Σ w(n) f(T_1^n x) g(T_2^n x) with T_1, T_2 commuting powers of a single transformation, for a class of admissible arithmetic weights including the von Mangoldt function, building on the Krause–Mirek–Tao multilinear circle method. This resolves part (a) (the von Mangoldt-weighted case for f(T^n x)g(T^{2n}x)). The analogous statement for general bounded multiplicative functions φ with convergent means on arithmetic progressions does not appear to have been fully established and seems to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Double Recurrence and Almost Sure Convergence: Primes and Weighted Theory
status_evidence.snippet: For any admissible weight w, including the von Mangoldt function, and any measure-preserving system with bounded f,g, the bilinear averages (1/N) Σ_{n≤N} w(n) T_1^n f · T_2^n g converge μ-almost surely.
status_evidence.claim: The von Mangoldt-weighted bilinear pointwise convergence (part (a)) has been established for powers T_1, T_2 of T.

status_evidence.title: Pointwise convergence of polynomial multiple ergodic averages along the primes
status_evidence.snippet: Pointwise a.e. convergence is established for polynomial multiple ergodic averages weighted by the von Mangoldt function Λ(n).
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work confirms pointwise convergence for von Mangoldt-weighted multilinear polynomial averages, addressing Problem 12 in the prime-weighted setting.

status_evidence.title: Pointwise convergence of ergodic averages with Möbius weight
status_evidence.snippet: Treats pointwise convergence of ergodic averages weighted by multiplicative functions such as the Möbius function.
status_evidence.claim: Multiplicative-function-weighted pointwise convergence is investigated, but a general statement covering arbitrary bounded multiplicative φ with convergent means on every arithmetic progression for the bilinear average is not established.
